content:
**Decision: use bookmarks, not `first-primary` everywhere; make the batch atomic; don't advertise lag/latest guarantees.**

**Documented facts**
- Without the Sessions API, all queries go to the primary; replication only helps when you opt into sessions ([worker-api/d1-database#withsession](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#withsession)).
- `withSession("first-primary")` sends only the *first* query to the primary; subsequent queries may use replicas, sequentially consistent. The proposal's "entire session pinned to primary" premise is wrong ([#parameters-4](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#parameters-4)).
- `withSession()` equals `first-unconstrained`: the first query may hit *any* instance, prioritizing latency; it does not guarantee latest data. The teammate's claim is wrong ([read-replication#start-a-session-without-constraints](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#start-a-session-without-constraints)).
- Passing a previous `session.getBookmark()` into `withSession(bookmark)` makes the new session at least as up-to-date as that bookmark, giving "read my own writes" across requests; writes still route to the primary regardless of constraint ([#start-a-session-from-previous-context-bookmark](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#start-a-session-from-previous-context-bookmark), [tutorial POST](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/tutorials/using-read-replication-for-e-com/#1-post-apiproduct)).
- `batch()` is a transaction: a failing statement "aborts or rolls back the entire sequence." The team's partial-commit expectation is wrong, so wrap the header plus line-item inserts in one batch and treat any error as whole-checkout failure ([d1-database#batch](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#batch)).
- `getBookmark()` returns `null` if no query ran ([#getbookmark](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#getbookmark)). The tutorial cautions retries can cause inconsistency, so only retry idempotently.

**Recommended contract**
- Checkout write request: `withSession("first-primary")` + one atomic batch; persist `getBookmark()` (cookie/header or server-side keyed to the order).
- Later checkout read: `withSession(bookmark)` so the replica waits until at least that version.
- Unrelated browse reads: `withSession()`/`first-unconstrained`.
- **Claims:** "globally latest reads" and "100 ms replica-lag maximum after commit" are unsupported — replicas are asynchronously updated and "may be arbitrarily out of date"; sequential consistency applies per session, not globally ([#primary-database-instance-vs-read-replicas](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#primary-database-instance-vs-read-replicas)). Any SLA claim is UNVERIFIED; resolve via Cloudflare support/contract, not docs.

3. withSession() or "first-unconstrained": first query to any instance (primary or replica); default; prioritizes latency; sequential consistency. The teammate's claim "always begins with the latest data" is wrong — first-unconstrained may start with stale data. (best-practices/read-replication#start-a-session-without-constraints)
4. The proposal "describe the entire session as pinned to the primary" is wrong: only the first query is directed to the primary; subsequent queries may use read replicas.
5. Bookmark: pass bookmark from previous session → session starts at least as up-to-date as bookmark; sequential consistency; "read my own writes" property. This is the correct mechanism for cross-request write context. The current code's problem: later HTTP request has no session context; use bookmark carried via cookie/header.
6. Batch: D1Database::batch — "D1 operates in auto-commit. Our implementation guarantees that each statement in the list will execute and commit, sequentially, non-concurrently. Batched statements are SQL transactions. If a statement in the sequence fails, then an error is returned for that specific statement, and it aborts or rolls back the entire sequence." → Team's expectation that earlier statements remain committed is wrong. So wrap in batch → atomic; partial results not expected. (worker-api/d1-database#batch)
7. Lag guarantee: docs say "at any given time, a read replica may be arbitrarily out of date"; replica lag unspecified. No 100ms guarantee. (best-practices/read-replication#primary-database-instance-vs-read-replicas)
8. Sequential consistency properties including "read my own writes" when bookmark used. (best-practices/read-replication#sessions-api-provides-sequential-consistency)
9. Bookmark from getBookmark() identifies latest version seen by last query; returns null if no queries executed. Bookmarks also used by Time Travel, lexicographically sortable, older than 30 days invalid. (time-travel#bookmarks, worker-api/d1-database#getbookmark)
10. Tutorial pattern: POST uses withSession("first-primary") and sets bookmark cookie; GETs use withSession(bookmark ?? "first-unconstrained") and refresh bookmark; writes always routed to primary regardless of constraint. (tutorial sections)
11. "Globally latest reads" not advertisable: read replicas are asynchronously replicated; with first-unconstrained reads may be stale. Only routing first query to primary or using a bookmark gives latest/at-least-as-up-to-date; and even first-primary only guarantees that first query; subsequent queries in session are sequential consistent (so still as-of bookmark, not global latest). Also there's no cross-session global freshness.
12. Note: sequential consistency means monotonic reads etc. within session; "first-primary" subsequent queries may use replicas but with bookmarks so at least as up-to-date as first query.
13. Also: replicas exist in every supported region — not a lag guarantee.

Also warn: retries can lead to duplicate writes — because batch is a transaction, a retry after ambiguous failure could duplicate. Doc: tutorial caution says retries can lead to data inconsistency. But keep within word budget.

Also: the current code using env.DB.prepare().run() and no session — all queries go to primary anyway; sessions needed for read replication. The write-then-read across requests with no session context loses "read my own writes" guarantee.

Also mention: bookmark must be stored durably (cookie/header) for cross-request context; getBookmark() in write request. Also note the first-primary can't be "pinned" for entire session.

Also session bookmark approach: for checkout's later request, use withSession(bookmark from checkout write) rather than first-primary; this lets the first read go to replica with wait for replication.

- Bookmarks: pass session.getBookmark() from the write request into the next request's withSession(bookmark); new session is at least as up-to-date as bookmark; gives "read my own writes"; write requests always routed to primary regardless of constraint. https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#start-a-session-from-previous-context-bookmark, https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/tutorials/using-read-replication-for-e-com/#1-post-apiproduct
- batch: transaction; failure aborts/rolls back the entire sequence → team's partial-commit expectation is wrong. To keep header + line items consistent, use batch and treat any error as whole-cart failure; retrying ambiguous failures risks duplicates. https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#batch-1 (batch section anchor is #batch actually; D1Database batch section is #batch, session batch is #batch-1). - getBookmark returns null if no query executed; bookmark identifies latest version seen. https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#getbookmark

Recommendation:
- Writes/checkout POST: withSession("first-primary"), batch header+line items, persist session.getBookmark() in cookie (or durable store keyed to cart) in the response.
